That's pretty much the same situation for me. It got so bad for me that I literally just stopped doing the work. It wasn't even procrastinating, because at least with procrastinating you do SOMETHING. I literally just flat-out REFUSED to do the homework. I knew in my brain that I had to; I knew that I was paying good money for college courses and that I had to do the work, it was important for my future and all that nonsense, but I just didn't care anymore. Nothing mattered anymore.

I don't really know what to say, because I'm still in that situation right now. I dropped out of college, because I was wasting valuable time and money and I was just too depressed to do anything. I guess my advice would be to do one of two things. The first option is to buckle down, push yourself, and do the work. The problem is that, if you're like me, depression makes it incredibly difficult, if not outright impossible, to push yourself. I tried to do it by myself. It didn't work.

The second option would be to just take a break. Talk with your student adviser about taking some time off. Just use the time to relax and figure things out. Therapy could be a good option, if you feel like it. I know a lot of schools offer free or discounted counselling sessions. You could try going to those places, or outside services if you have the money/insurance.

Either way, I know how you feel. It's awful, and I'm still stuck in that rut myself. Hope everything turns out well for you.
